title: feat(spec,plugin-approvals,app-shell): the approvals get serves a request's own route, and both approval step lines draw it
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB7EoNpfhCGLSFBvVvp6hb9f)_
Fixes #26668

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — `flow_route` is a served read member of the approvals API, not anything a metadata author writes; no skill teaches `flow_steps` (`git grep` over `skills/` and `content/docs/`: 0 hits), and the approvals guide gains a paragraph naming `flow_route` here (`content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`)

Nothing is left of #26563, which #26666 already completed: the part #26666 had to drop, the request page's line, is drawn again here.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:审批单读取(`GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/:id`)新增 `flow_route`:本单所在流程运行已经走过的审批步骤(取自同一次运行自己的审批单行,不取流程图)、本单当前步骤,以及仅对待审单、仅在流程图自己就能确定时列出的后续步骤;遇到尚未决定的分支即停,并以 `ahead: 'undecided'` 明说。`flow_steps`(流程图主干)原样保留,文档写明步骤线不画它。业务记录审批面板与审批单页面都改画 `flow_route`;#26666 的客户端临时方案 `visitedApprovalSteps` 和审批单页「不画步骤线」的规则一并删除。
- **为什么改**:合同审批走「直属上级 → 仅财务」时,服务端只给主干「直属上级 · 法务 + 财务会签 · 分管领导 · 总经理」,全部是「待办」,本单所在的「财务」根本不在其中。#26666 只能让页面不画;现在由服务端给出本单真实路线,两处步骤线恢复。
- **风险与回滚**:契约是新增字段(加宽),`flow_steps` 字节不变,老客户端不受影响;每次单条读取多一次按 `flow_run_id` 的查询(最多 1000 行,系统身份)。业务记录面板上,未参与前序步骤的查看者现在也能看到这些步骤(以前因列表读只给参与者而缺失);步骤名与主干原本就已对同一读者可见。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- **先看**:① `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-route.ts` 的 `stepsAhead`(哪些节点会让后续步骤停为 undecided);② `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` 的 `flow_route` 文档(契约原文);③ `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/flow-route.integration.test.ts`(真实引擎上的报告路线)。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run src/flow-route.integration.test.ts`,预期 6 个测试全绿,其中报告路线的 `flow_route` 只有「Manager(done)· Finance(current)」两步,`ahead` 为 `undecided`。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

**Measured first, on `origin/main` `7a2818c5`.**

- The served row. `attachFlowSteps` walks the graph from `start`, taking `approve`, else `true`, else the first edge, and states each step against that one trunk. On the real engine, a `contract_approval`-shaped flow routed manager → finance only serves `flow_steps` with every trunk entry `upcoming` and `finance_only` absent (pinned as the first assertion of the reported-route case below, green on both sides on purpose). A route that rejoins the trunk (manager → legal only → executive) is served the joint rung as `done`, a rung the run never visited.
- The history the row can draw from. The request row names its run (`flow_run_id`), its node (`flow_node_id`), `status` and `created_at`; every step the run opened is its own `sys_approval_request` row with the same four. The automation engine writes no step log for a run while it is paused (`ApprovalResumeSurface.getRun`: "the engine writes no execution-log entry until a run reaches a terminal state"), so the run's own request rows are the only history there is. The route is read from them.
- The readers. After #26666 no surface draws `flow_steps`: the record approvals panel rebuilt its line client-side from the list read (`visitedApprovalSteps`), and the request page drew no line. Its other readers are type declarations only: `ApprovalRequestLite` (app-shell `useRecordApprovals.ts`), `ApprovalStepLine`'s step type, and the console's `approvalsApi.ts` row type. No API doc or skill names it.

**The shape, option (a): `flow_steps` stays the trunk, and `ApprovalRequestRow.flow_route` is added.** Why not (b), redefining `flow_steps`: the field ships in published contracts and clients outside this tree may read it as the trunk, so redefining it changes the meaning of a served member under them. Adding a member leaves every existing reader byte-identical. The two fields do disagree off the trunk, so the contract says which one a step line reads: `flow_steps`' doc now says it is the trunk and that a step line draws `flow_route`, never it. Clause-② consequence: an added optional member of a published contract, `yes (widening)`. Metadata-protocol consequence: none. The member is served by a read, and nothing a metadata author writes changes (the claim's provisional `added` assumed an authorable key; re-judged from the diff, following #26361's `yes (widening)` / `none` for an added approvals read).

**`flow_route` (contract text in `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts`).**

- `done`: earlier requests of the same run, on another node, `approved`, in the order the run opened them. A node approved in several rounds is listed once, at its latest round. These are the rules `visitedApprovalSteps` had, now on the server, read over every row of the run, not the viewer's list read.
- The request's own node: `done` once approved, else `current`, as `flow_steps` marks it.
- `upcoming`, for a pending request only: from the node's `approve` edges on, through nodes with exactly one non-fault out-edge and no condition. **What I chose for steps after the current one, and why:** the walk lists a step only when the graph alone puts it on this request's path once each step approves. It stops at a `decision`, a conditioned edge, several out-edges (a fan-out has no one order), a loop back, a missing node, or a node that runs other nodes (`subflow`, `map`, `loop`, or any node with regions). Evaluating a gateway's condition against the record now would be a guess: the record or the run's variables can change before the run gets there, and conditions can read outputs of decisions not yet made. Assuming each step approves is the reading a progress line has always had; a reject edge ends the request rather than routing it.
- `ahead`: `end` (the walk reached the flow's end), `undecided` (it stopped at a branch; nothing past it is listed, and the trunk is never listed in its place), `decided` (the request is decided; its route ends at itself).
- Single reads only, like `flow_steps`: `listRequests` serves neither. The run's rows are read as the system: the route carries step ids, labels and states, which `flow_steps` already served to the same reader.

**Producer.** `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-route.ts` holds the rule as three pure functions (`passedSteps`, `stepsAhead`, `flowRoute`). `ApprovalService.attachFlowRoute` reads the run's rows and calls it from `attachFlowSteps`, on the one flow lookup. Steps are named as `flow_steps` names them (#24863): the reader's label, else the node's authored label, else the label the step's request stored.

**Readers.**

- `RecordApprovalsPanel` draws `pendingRequest.flow_route.steps`. `visitedApprovalSteps` is deleted.
- `ApprovalDecisionPanel` (the request page, `record:approval_decision`) draws `request.flow_route.steps` again, below the snapshot summary and above the tally, at any status. The no-line rule is deleted.
- `ApprovalStepLine`'s markup is unchanged; its step type is now `flow_route`'s, and its header says both callers hand it the served route.
- `ApprovalRequestLite` and the console's row type declare `flow_route`; the app-shell README and the approvals guide say the same.

## Tests

- **Real service path, new `flow-route.integration.test.ts` (6).** A real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` (sqlite), the real `AutomationEngine` with its logic nodes, the real approval node and `ApprovalService`; every request opened by the engine, every decision resuming the run. A `contract_approval`-shaped flow (manager, then a gateway to joint / legal only / finance only / none, then an executive above 500000, then a general manager above 1000000) and a linear three-step flow.
  - Off the trunk, manager → finance only: `flow_route` is manager `done`, finance `current`, `ahead: 'undecided'` (the executive gateway is next), and none of the trunk's rungs. `flow_steps` is served as before (all `upcoming`, own node absent).
  - At the first step, a gateway right after it: `[manager current]`, `undecided`, never the trunk's joint rung.
  - A branch that rejoins the trunk: manager, legal only (`done`), executive (`current`); the trunk still says the joint rung was `done`.
  - A decided request: its route ends at itself, every step `done`, `ahead: 'decided'`.
  - On the trunk (the linear flow): at every step `flow_route.steps` deep-equals `flow_steps`, `ahead: 'end'`.
  - The list read serves neither member.
- **The rule, new `approval-route.test.ts` (16).** `passedSteps`: order, outcomes that are not a pass (`returned`, `rejected`, `pending`, `cancelled`), rows opened later, the current node's earlier rounds, round dedup, rows with no node or time. `stepsAhead`: a linear tail (`end`), a non-approval node crossed, and each stop (`decision` even with one edge, conditioned edge, fan-out, `subflow` / `map` / `loop` / regions, loop back, missing node), fault edges ignored. `flowRoute`: pending, decided at each outcome, no node.
- **ui (re-pinned or removed).**
  - `RecordApprovalsPanel.visitedRoute-26563.test.tsx` is **removed**, with the function it pinned. `RecordApprovalsPanel.servedRoute-26668.test.tsx` **replaces** it (5): the reported route drawn as served with no trunk rung, upcoming steps drawn muted and numbered, a viewer the list serves only the pending row still sees the whole route, a server that serves no route draws no line whatever the trunk reads, a one-step route draws none.
  - `RecordApprovalsPanel.stepProgressVertical.test.tsx` **re-pinned**: its fixtures are served routes again (done, current, upcoming), and the connector-tint case pins the upcoming segment's `bg-border` again.
  - `ApprovalDecisionPanel.stepLine-12491.test.tsx` **re-pinned** from "no line" to the drawn route: the reported row draws manager → finance and none of the trunk's other rungs; a decided row draws its route; a row with no route draws nothing; the line sits above the tally and the tally above the decisions.
  - `approvalRequestsDataSource.servedPageStepLine-12491.test.tsx` (console, the real served page) **re-pinned**: the off-trunk row draws its served three-step route, current marked, and none of the trunk's other rungs; a row with no route draws none; decided and person-submitted rows draw their routes; a one-step route draws none.

## Acceptance notes

- **The line does not mark an undecided tail.** When `ahead` is `undecided` the line ends at the last listed step, as the #26666 line ended at the pending step. Drawing a "decided later" marker needs a new `approvalsInbox.*` pack row in every locale; it is left out of this diff. The served row says it; whether the line shows it is a ui follow-up if wanted.
- **Who sees which steps changed on the record panel.** The client-side rebuild could only draw rows the list read served the viewer (participants only), so a finance controller saw a one-step line, which draws nothing. The served route lists the run's passed steps to anyone who can read the request. These are step ids, labels and states; `flow_steps` already served every step label of the flow, with `done` states along the trunk, to the same reader.
- **A step a reject edge routes to, or a rung sent back for revision, is not `done`.** Only `approved` rows count as passed, the rule `visitedApprovalSteps` had. A route through a rejected rung shows only its approved rungs.
- **Ordering** is by the run's `created_at` on its request rows. Two requests of one run opened in the same millisecond would order by the store's answer; a run opens its next request only after the previous decision, so this needs a sub-millisecond decide-and-resume.
- `flow_steps` keeps its producer and its pins (`approval-service.test.ts`, `reader-locale-display-labels.integration.test.ts`) unchanged.
